subject: PO header constraints and how they affect discount slabs / invoice packaging
messages:
From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@genomeix.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO header / invoice packaging questions for upcoming commitment

Hi Mina / Vanessa —

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Our procurement team is trying to lock down the PO and invoicing constraints before Legal signs the SOW. A few items we need your confirmation on because they will affect whether we qualify for the tiered discount you proposed: 

- PO header: our finance system requires the PO number to appear in the first invoice header line and the invoice must include the PO line ID for every billable item. We cannot accept consolidated invoices that omit PO line mapping.
- Invoice cadence: our default is monthly consolidated statements, but discounts are applied per PO line based on usage windows. If you deliver consolidated month-end invoices, we need a per-PO breakdown in the invoice body.
- Net terms / payment triggers: we typically run Net45; Net30 requires pre-approval. Discounts that are conditional on monthly thresholds are prorated if billing is split. Please confirm whether Redwood can: (a) include PO line IDs in invoice headers, (b) provide an itemized per-PO breakdown when issuing consolidated statements, and (c) support Net45 as standard.

I attached our standard PO (PO_template.xlsx) and the draft PO you mentioned in the demo (Genomeix_PO_12345.pdf). Can you return an example Redwood invoice template that maps to our fields (entity ID, PO line, tax/VAT)? We want to avoid rework with our AP system.

Appreciate a quick read — procurement needs this clarified before we move the deal to Legal.

Best,
Sarah Chen
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Genomeix Therapeutics
procurement@genomeix.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@genomeix.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO header / invoice packaging questions for upcoming commitment

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list and the attachments. Short answers up front: yes on PO number in the first invoice header line; yes on including PO line IDs; and Net45 as our default for enterprise onboarding. A few implementation notes and options so you can pick what works for Genomeix: 

1) Invoice format: We can produce two invoice flavors —
   - Per-PO-line invoices (one invoice per PO line) — works natively with strict AP systems, no per-PO breakdown required.
   - Consolidated monthly statement — one invoice with a tabular section that lists each PO line, line-level usage, unit pricing, discount applied, and entity ID. This satisfies your consolidated preference so long as the table is present.

2) Discount slabs & proration: If discounts are based on monthly thresholds, we’ll apply them at the PO-line level. For split billing (e.g., weekly invoices against a single PO line), we will prorate the discount for that invoice period and then true-up on the consolidated month-end statement. We can include a short calculation appendix showing the proration methodology.

3) Net terms: Net45 is acceptable. If Genomeix needs Net30, that requires finance sign-off and an early-pay fee discussion.

I attached our Redwood_PO_Guidelines.pdf which has the sample consolidated invoice and a per-PO-line invoice example mapped to common AP fields (entity id, tax, PO line id, ledger tag).

Next steps: could you confirm which invoice flavor you prefer (per-PO-line vs consolidated with table) and whether your tax/VAT needs differ by entity? If you confirm consolidated-with-table, we’ll send a one-page invoice mapping that your AP team can test with a small starter invoice.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@genomeix.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO header / invoice packaging questions for upcoming commitment

Thanks Mina — this is helpful. Quick clarifications from our AP team after they reviewed your guidelines: 

- We prefer consolidated monthly statements (fewer payment runs). However, to grant the higher tier discount (10% at $75k/month), our system needs an unambiguous mapping back to PO line IDs for each discounted unit. The consolidated table approach you described will work if the table includes: PO number, PO line id, usage units, unit price, discount applied (both % and $), and net line amount.
- Tax / VAT: Genomeix has two legal entities (US and EU) that will be billed separately. We need the invoice to include the billing entity name and tax id in the header so our AP can route correctly.
- True-up: the proration + month-end true-up approach is acceptable. We will need a short statement in the invoice footer that says how true-ups are handled for discount slabs.

Attached is our signed PO (Genomeix_PO_12345.pdf) — Legal has provisionally approved once the invoice mapping is confirmed. Hoping to avoid contract redlines.

If Redwood can provide a stub consolidated invoice (one page) mapped to our fields by end of day Monday, we’ll kick off a test run with AP next week. Also — if Redwood is willing to offer a one-time onboarding credit (applied to the first invoice) as a gesture for the extra AP work, that would speed approval on our side. Can you flag whether that is possible?

Best,
Sarah

Date: Sat, 22 May 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO header / invoice packaging questions for upcoming commitment

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the signed PO. I’m Vanessa (Finance, Redwood) — looping in Jonas from Legal for visibility. We can do the hybrid approach you and Mina outlined: consolidated monthly invoice with a clear per-PO-line table and footer language describing the true-up/proration mechanics. A few confirmations: 

- Billing entities: we will issue separate line-itemed sections within the same PDF invoice for US vs EU entities, each with the corresponding tax ID in the header. That will allow Genomeix AP to route payments correctly.
- Discounting: Redwood will apply the discount at PO-line level. We will include a 1-line calculation example in the appendix for transparency.

Onboarding credit: We can offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 50% of the first month’s committed discount uplift (capped at $7,500). This will appear as a negative line on the first consolidated invoice once the AP test run is successful.

Action items:
- Mina / Jonas: I’ll need the sample consolidated invoice (mapped to Genomeix fields) and the footer true-up wording by Monday COB so Genomeix can run a test with AP on Tuesday.
- Sarah: please confirm the two legal entity billing names and tax IDs (or provide AP contact) so we can build the mapping.

If both sides agree, I’ll have Legal add the invoice mapping annex as an addendum to the SOW (small redline) purely for AP routing — shouldn’t affect commercial terms.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

– Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
